Demecser New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Demecser, Hungary

Not demolished. The newer of two Jewish cemeteries in Demecser, established around 1927 based on tombstone dating, remained active until at least 1944. Demecser's Jewish community, first recorded in 1770, declared itself Orthodox in 1869 and gained independence in 1880; members worked prominently in commerce (beverages, ironmongery, produce), local government, medicine, and even operated a soda factory, with some serving as landowners. Population grew from 148 (1880) to 386 by 1930; ten local Jews died in WWI service. From 1938, authorities revoked industrial licenses and confiscated land; by 1944, the community numbered 334 (52 taxpayers), running its own elementary school with one teacher and 52 students. Deportation to the already-overcrowded Nyíregyháza Ghetto forced residents onward to Varjúlapos, where they lacked food, water, and sanitation, before deportation to Auschwitz just before Shavuot. Ten men survived forced labor and a handful of others returned from the camps to find the synagogue ruined and cemetery destroyed; by 1963, no Jews remained in Demecser.
